text_el: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρά, οὗ ἦν τεθραμμένος, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν κατὰ τὸ εἰωθὸς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν, καὶ ἀνέστη ἀναγνῶναι.

text_en: And the book of Isaiah the prophet was delivered unto him. And as he unfolded the book, he found the place where it was written:
text_la: Et traditus est illi liber Isaiæ prophetæ. Et ut revolvit librum, invenit locum ubi scriptum erat:
text_pt: E foi-lhe dado o livro do profeta Isaías; e, quando abriu o livro, achou o lugar em que estava escrito:
text_el: καὶ ἐπεδόθη αὐτῷ βιβλίον τοῦ προφήτου Ἠσαΐου, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ βιβλίον εὗρεν [τὸν] τόπον οὗ ἦν γεγραμμένον:

text_en: The spirit of the Lord is upon me. Wherefore he has anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, he has sent me to heal the contrite of heart,
text_la: Spiritus Domini super me : propter quod unxit me, evangelizare pauperibus misit me, sanare contritos corde,
text_pt: O Espírito do Senhor é sobre mim, Pois que me ungiu para evangelizar os pobres. Enviou-me a curar os quebrantados de coração,
text_el: πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπ' ἐμέ, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέν με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, ἀπέσταλκέν με κηρύξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν καὶ τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει,

text_en: to preach deliverance to the captives and sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of reward.
text_la: prædicare captivis remissionem, et cæcis visum, dimittere confractos in remissionem, prædicare annum Domini acceptum et diem retributionis.
text_pt: A pregar liberdade aos cativos, E restauração da vista aos cegos, A pôr em liberdade os oprimidos, A anunciar o ano aceitável do Senhor.
text_el: κηρύξαι ἐνιαυτὸν κυρίου δεκτόν.

text_en: And when he had folded the book, he restored it to the minister and sat down. And the eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed on him.
text_la: Et cum plicuisset librum, reddit ministro, et sedit. Et omnium in synagoga oculi erant intendentes in eum.
text_pt: E, cerrando o livro, e tornando-o a dar ao ministro, assentou-se; e os olhos de todos na sinagoga estavam fitos nele.
text_el: καὶ πτύξας τὸ βιβλίον ἀποδοὺς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ ἐκάθισεν, καὶ πάντων οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦσαν ἀτενίζοντες αὐτῷ.

text_en: And he began to say to them: This day is fulfilled this scripture in your ears.
text_la: Cœpit autem dicere ad illos : Quia hodie impleta est hæc scriptura in auribus vestris.
text_pt: Então começou a dizer-lhes: Hoje se cumpriu esta Escritura em vossos ouvidos.
text_el: ἤρξατο δὲ λέγειν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι σήμερον πεπλήρωται ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν ὑμῶν.

text_en: And all gave testimony to him. And they wondered at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth. And they said: Is not this the son of Joseph ?
text_la: Et omnes testimonium illi dabant : et mirabantur in verbis gratiæ, quæ procedebant de ore ipsius, et dicebant : Nonne hic est filius Joseph?
text_pt: E todos lhe davam testemunho, e se maravilhavam das palavras de graça que saíam da sua boca; e diziam: Não é este o filho de José?
text_el: καὶ πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς χάριτος τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον: οὐχὶ υἱός ἐστιν Ἰωσὴφ οὗτος;

text_en: And he said to them: Doubtless you will say to me this similitude: Physician, heal yourself. As great things as we have heard done in Capharnaum , do also here in your own country.
text_la: Et ait illis : Utique dicetis mihi hanc similitudinem : Medice cura teipsum : quanta audivimus facta in Capharnaum, fac et hic in patria tua.
text_pt: E ele lhes disse: Sem dúvida me direis este provérbio: Médico, cura-te a ti mesmo; faze também aqui na tua pátria tudo que ouvimos ter sido feito em Cafarnaum.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς: πάντως ἐρεῖτέ μοι τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην: ἰατρέ, θεράπευσον σεαυτόν: ὅσα ἠκούσαμεν γενόμενα εἰς τὴν Καφαρναοὺμ ποίησον καὶ ὧδε ἐν τῇ πατρίδι σου.

text_en: And he said: Amen I say to you that no prophet is accepted in his own country.
text_la: Ait autem : Amen dico vobis, quia nemo propheta acceptus est in patria sua.
text_pt: E disse: Em verdade vos digo que nenhum profeta é bem recebido na sua pátria.
text_el: εἶπεν δέ: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς προφήτης δεκτός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ.

text_en: In truth I say to You, there were many widows in the days of Elias in Israel , when heaven was shut up three years and six months, when there was a great famine throughout all the earth.
text_la: In veritate dico vobis, multæ viduæ erant in diebus Eliæ in Israël, quando clausum est cælum annis tribus et mensibus sex, cum facta esset fames magna in omni terra:
text_pt: Em verdade vos digo que muitas viúvas existiam em Israel nos dias de Elias, quando o céu se cerrou por três anos e seis meses, de sorte que em toda a terra houve grande fome;
text_el: ἐπ' ἀληθείας δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν πολλαὶ χῆραι ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἠλίου ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτε ἐκλείσθη ὁ οὐρανὸς ἔτη τρία καὶ μῆνας ἕξ, ὡς ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν,

text_en: And to none of them was Elias sent, but to Sarepta of Sidon , to a widow woman .
text_la: et ad nullam illarum missus est Elias, nisi in Sarepta Sidoniæ, ad mulierem viduam.
text_pt: E a nenhuma delas foi enviado Elias, senão a Sarepta de Sidom, a uma mulher viúva.
text_el: καὶ πρὸς οὐδεμίαν αὐτῶν ἐπέμφθη Ἠλίας εἰ μὴ εἰς Σάρεπτα τῆς Σιδωνίας πρὸς γυναῖκα χήραν.

text_en: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet : and none of them was cleansed but Naaman the Syrian .
text_la: Et multi leprosi erant in Israël sub Eliseo propheta : et nemo eorum mundatus est nisi Naaman Syrus.
text_pt: E muitos leprosos havia em Israel no tempo do profeta Eliseu, e nenhum deles foi purificado, senão Naamã, o siro.
text_el: καὶ πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπὶ Ἐλισαίου τοῦ προφήτου, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκαθαρίσθη εἰ μὴ Ναιμὰν ὁ Σύρος.

text_en: And all they in the synagogue , hearing these things, were filled with anger .
text_la: Et repleti sunt omnes in synagoga ira, hæc audientes.
text_pt: E todos, na sinagoga, ouvindo estas coisas, se encheram de ira.
text_el: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες θυμοῦ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούοντες ταῦτα,

text_en: And they rose up and thrust him out of the city: and they brought him to the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
text_la: Et surrexerunt, et ejecerunt illum extra civitatem : et duxerunt illum usque ad supercilium montis, super quem civitas illorum erat ædificata, ut præcipitarent eum.
text_pt: E, levantando-se, o expulsaram da cidade, e o levaram até ao cume do monte em que a cidade deles estava edificada, para dali o precipitarem.
text_el: καὶ ἀναστάντες ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἕως ὀφρύος τοῦ ὄρους ἐφ' οὗ ἡ πόλις ᾠκοδόμητο αὐτῶν, ὥστε κατακρημνίσαι αὐτόν:

text_en: But he passing through the midst of them, went his way.
text_la: Ipse autem transiens per medium illorum, ibat.
text_pt: Ele, porém, passando pelo meio deles, retirou-se.
text_el: αὐτὸς δὲ διελθὼν διὰ μέσου αὐτῶν ἐπορεύετο.

text_en: And he went down into Capharnaum , a city of Galilee : and there he taught them on the sabbath days .
text_la: Et descendit in Capharnaum civitatem Galilææ, ibique docebat illos sabbatis.
text_pt: E desceu a Cafarnaum, cidade da Galiléia, e os ensinava nos sábados.
text_el: Καὶ κατῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν:

text_en: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his speech was with power.
text_la: Et stupebant in doctrina ejus, quia in potestate erat sermo ipsius.
text_pt: E admiravam a sua doutrina porque a sua palavra era com autoridade.
text_el: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ ἦν ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And in the synagogue there was a man who had an unclean devil : and he cried out with a loud voice,
text_la: Et in synagoga erat homo habens dæmonium immundum, et exclamavit voce magna,
text_pt: E estava na sinagoga um homem que tinha o espírito de um demônio imundo, e exclamou em alta voz,
text_el: Καὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἔχων πνεῦμα δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, καὶ ἀνέκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ:

text_en: saying: Let us alone. What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth ? Are you come to destroy us? I know you who you are, the holy one of God .
text_la: dicens : Sine, quid nobis et tibi, Jesu Nazarene? venisti perdere nos? scio te quis sis, Sanctus Dei.
text_pt: Dizendo: Ah! que temos nós contigo, Jesus Nazareno? Vieste a destruir-nos? Bem sei quem és: O Santo de Deus.
text_el: ἔα, τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ; ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς; οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.

text_en: And Jesus rebuked him, saying: Hold your peace and go out of him. And when the devil had thrown him into the midst, he went out of him and hurt him not at all.
text_la: Et increpavit illum Jesus, dicens : Obmutesce, et exi ab eo. Et cum projecisset illum dæmonium in medium, exiit ab illo, nihilque illum nocuit.
text_pt: E Jesus o repreendeu, dizendo: Cala-te, e sai dele. E o demônio, lançando-o por terra no meio do povo, saiu dele sem lhe fazer mal.
text_el: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων: φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἀπ' αὐτοῦ. καὶ ῥίψαν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον εἰς τὸ μέσον ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ μηδὲν βλάψαν αὐτόν.

text_en: And there came fear upon all; and they talked among themselves, saying: What word is this, for with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits , and they go out?
text_la: Et factus est pavor in omnibus, et colloquebantur ad invicem, dicentes : Quod est hoc verbum, quia in potestate et virtute imperat immundis spiritibus, et exeunt?
text_pt: E veio espanto sobre todos, e falavam uns com os outros, dizendo: Que palavra é esta, que até aos espíritos imundos manda com autoridade e poder, e eles saem?
text_el: καὶ ἐγένετο θάμβος ἐπὶ πάντας, καὶ συνελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες: τίς ὁ λόγος οὗτος, ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ καὶ δυνάμει ἐπιτάσσει τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις πνεύμασιν, καὶ ἐξέρχονται;

text_en: And the fame of him was published into every place of the country.
text_la: Et divulgabatur fama de illo in omnem locum regionis.
text_pt: E a sua fama divulgava-se por todos os lugares, em redor daquela comarca.
text_el: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο ἦχος περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς πάντα τόπον τῆς περιχώρου.

text_en: And Jesus rising up out of the synagogue , went into Simon's house. And Simon's wife's mother was taken with a great fever: and they besought him for her.
text_la: Surgens autem Jesus de synagoga, introivit in domum Simonis. Socrus autem Simonis tenebatur magnis febribus : et rogaverunt illum pro ea.
text_pt: Ora, levantando-se Jesus da sinagoga, entrou em casa de Simão; e a sogra de Simão estava enferma com muita febre, e rogaram-lhe por ela.
text_el: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος. πενθερὰ δὲ τοῦ Σίμωνος ἦν συνεχομένη πυρετῷ μεγάλῳ, καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν περὶ αὐτῆς.

text_en: And standing over her, he commanded the fever: and it left her. And immediately rising, she ministered to them.
text_la: Et stans super illam imperavit febri : et dimisit illam. Et continuo surgens, ministrabat illis.
text_pt: E, inclinando-se para ela, repreendeu a febre, e esta a deixou. E ela, levantando-se logo, servia-os.
text_el: καὶ ἐπιστὰς ἐπάνω αὐτῆς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πυρετῷ, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτήν: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἀναστᾶσα διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.

text_en: And when the sun was down, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them to him. But he, laying his hands on every one of them, healed them.
text_la: Cum autem sol occidisset, omnes qui habebant infirmos variis languoribus, ducebant illos ad eum. At ille singulis manus imponens, curabat eos.
text_pt: E, ao pôr do sol, todos os que tinham enfermos de várias doenças lhos traziam; e, pondo as mãos sobre cada um deles, os curava.
text_el: Δύνοντος δὲ τοῦ ἡλίου ἅπαντες ὅσοι εἶχον ἀσθενοῦντας νόσοις ποικίλαις ἤγαγον αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτόν: ὁ δὲ ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιτιθεὶς ἐθεράπευεν αὐτούς.

text_en: And devils went out from many, crying out and saying: You are the son of God . And rebuking them he suffered them not to speak; for they knew that he was Christ .
text_la: Exibant autem dæmonia a multis clamantia, et dicentia : Quia tu es Filius Dei : et increpans non sinebat ea loqui : quia sciebant ipsum esse Christum.
text_pt: E também de muitos saíam demônios, clamando e dizendo: Tu és o Cristo, o Filho de Deus. E ele, repreendendo-os, não os deixava falar, pois sabiam que ele era o Cristo.
text_el: ἐξήρχετο δὲ καὶ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ πολλῶν, κράζοντα καὶ λέγοντα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ ἐπιτιμῶν οὐκ εἴα αὐτὰ λαλεῖν, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν τὸν Χριστὸν αὐτὸν εἶναι.

text_en: And when it was day, going out he went into a desert place : and the multitudes sought him, and came unto him. And they stayed him that should not depart from them.
text_la: Facta autem die egressus ibat in desertum locum, et turbæ requirebant eum, et venerunt usque ad ipsum : et detinebant illum ne discederet ab eis.
text_pt: E, sendo já dia, saiu, e foi para um lugar deserto; e a multidão o procurava, e chegou junto dele; e o detinham, para que não se ausentasse deles.
text_el: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἔρημον τόπον, καὶ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπεζήτουν αὐτόν: καὶ ἦλθον ἕως αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατεῖχον αὐτὸν τοῦ μὴ πορεύεσθαι ἀπ' αὐτῶν.

text_en: To whom he said: To other cities also I must preach the kingdom of God : for therefore am I sent.
text_la: Quibus ille ait : Quia et aliis civitatibus oportet me evangelizare regnum Dei : quia ideo missus sum.
text_pt: Ele, porém, lhes disse: Também é necessário que eu anuncie a outras cidades o evangelho do reino de Deus; porque para isso fui enviado.
text_el: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι καὶ ταῖς ἑτέραις πόλεσιν εὐαγγελίσασθαί με δεῖ τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ἐπὶ τοῦτο ἀπεστάλην.

text_en: And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee .
text_la: Et erat prædicans in synagogis Galilææ.
text_pt: E pregava nas sinagogas da Galiléia.
text_el: καὶ ἦν κηρύσσων εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς τῆς Ἰουδαίας.

text_en: And it came to pass, that when the multitudes pressed upon him to hear the word of God , he stood by the lake of Genesareth ,
text_la: Factum est autem, cum turbæ irruerunt in eum ut audirent verbum Dei, et ipse stabat secus stagnum Genesareth.
text_pt: E aconteceu que, apertando-o a multidão, para ouvir a palavra de Deus, estava ele junto ao lago de Genesaré;
text_el: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ,

text_en: and saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.
text_la: Et vidit duas naves stantes secus stagnum : piscatores autem descenderant, et lavabant retia.
text_pt: E viu estar dois barcos junto à praia do lago; e os pescadores, havendo descido deles, estavam lavando as redes.
text_el: καὶ εἶδεν πλοῖα δύο ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην: οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ἀπ' αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.

text_en: And going into one of the ships that was Simon's , he desired him to draw back a little from the land. And sitting, he taught the multitudes out of the ship.
text_la: Ascendens autem in unam navim, quæ erat Simonis, rogavit eum a terra reducere pusillum. Et sedens docebat de navicula turbas.
text_pt: E, entrando num dos barcos, que era o de Simão, pediu-lhe que o afastasse um pouco da terra; e, assentando-se, ensinava do barco a multidão.
text_el: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον, καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους.

text_en: Now when he had ceased to speak, he said to Simon : Launch out into the deep and let down your nets for a draught.
text_la: Ut cessavit autem loqui, dixit ad Simonem : Duc in altum, et laxate retia vestra in capturam.
text_pt: E, quando acabou de falar, disse a Simão: Faze-te ao mar alto, e lançai as vossas redes para pescar.
text_el: ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα: ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.

text_en: And Simon answering said to him: Master, we have laboured all the night and have taken nothing: but at your word I will let down the net.
text_la: Et respondens Simon, dixit illi : Præceptor, per totam noctem laborantes nihil cepimus : in verbo autem tuo laxabo rete.
text_pt: E, respondendo Simão, disse-lhe: Mestre, havendo trabalhado toda a noite, nada apanhamos; mas, sobre a tua palavra, lançarei a rede.
text_el: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν: ἐπιστάτα, δι' ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν: ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα.

text_en: And when they had done this, they enclosed a very great multitude of fishes: and their net broke.
text_la: Et cum hoc fecissent, concluserunt piscium multitudinem copiosam : rumpebatur autem rete eorum.
text_pt: E, fazendo assim, colheram uma grande quantidade de peixes, e rompia-se-lhes a rede.
text_el: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ: διερρήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν.

text_en: And they beckoned to their partners that were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came and filled both the ships, so that they were almost sinking.
text_la: Et annuerunt sociis, qui erant in alia navi, ut venirent, et adjuvarent eos. Et venerunt, et impleverunt ambas naviculas, ita ut pene mergerentur.
text_pt: E fizeram sinal aos companheiros que estavam no outro barco, para que os fossem ajudar. E foram, e encheram ambos os barcos, de maneira tal que quase iam a pique.
text_el: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς: καὶ ἦλθον, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα, ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.

text_en: Which when Simon Peter saw, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying: Depart from me, for I am a sinful man , O Lord.
text_la: Quod cum videret Simon Petrus, procidit ad genua Jesu, dicens : Exi a me, quia homo peccator sum, Domine.
text_pt: E vendo isto Simão Pedro, prostrou-se aos pés de Jesus, dizendo: Senhor, ausenta-te de mim, que sou um homem pecador.
text_el: ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων: ἔξελθε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε.

text_en: For he was wholly astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken.
text_la: Stupor enim circumdederat eum, et omnes qui cum illo erant, in captura piscium, quam ceperant:
text_pt: Pois que o espanto se apoderara dele, e de todos os que com ele estavam, por causa da pesca de peixe que haviam feito.
text_el: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ὧν συνέλαβον,

text_en: And so were also James and John , the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. And Jesus says to Simon : Fear not: from henceforth you shall catch men .
text_la: similiter autem Jacobum et Joannem, filios Zebedæi, qui erant socii Simonis. Et ait ad Simonem Jesus : Noli timere : ex hoc jam homines eris capiens.
text_pt: E, de igual modo, também de Tiago e João, filhos de Zebedeu, que eram companheiros de Simão. E disse Jesus a Simão: Não temas; de agora em diante serás pescador de homens.
text_el: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι. καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα Ἰησοῦς: μὴ φοβοῦ: ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.

text_en: And having brought their ships to land, leaving all things, they followed him.
text_la: Et subductis ad terram navibus, relictis omnibus, secuti sunt eum.
text_pt: E, levando os barcos para terra, deixaram tudo, e o seguiram.
text_el: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.

text_en: And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy who, seeing Jesus and falling on his face, besought him saying: Lord, if you will, you can make me clean .
text_la: Et factum est, cum esset in una civitatum, et ecce vir plenus lepra, et videns Jesum, et procidens in faciem, rogavit eum, dicens : Domine, si vis, potes me mundare.
text_pt: E aconteceu que, quando estava numa daquelas cidades, eis que um homem cheio de lepra, vendo a Jesus, prostrou-se sobre o rosto, e rogou-lhe, dizendo: Senhor, se quiseres, bem podes limpar-me.
text_el: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας: ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν, πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων: κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς, δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.

text_en: And stretching forth his hand, he touched him, saying: I will. Be cleansed. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.
text_la: Et extendens manum, tetigit eum dicens : Volo : mundare. Et confestim lepra discessit ab illo.
text_pt: E ele, estendendo a mão, tocou-lhe, dizendo: Quero, sê limpo. E logo a lepra desapareceu dele.
text_el: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ λέγων: θέλω, καθαρίσθητι. καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And he charged him that he should tell no man , but: Go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing according as Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.
text_la: Et ipse præcepit illi ut nemini diceret : sed, Vade, ostende te sacerdoti, et offer pro emundatione tua, sicut præcepit Moyses, in testimonium illis.
text_pt: E ordenou-lhe que a ninguém o dissesse. Mas vai, disse, mostra-te ao sacerdote, e oferece pela tua purificação, o que Moisés determinou para que lhes sirva de testemunho.
text_el: καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς, εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

text_en: But the fame of him went abroad the more: and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
text_la: Perambulabat autem magis sermo de illo : et conveniebant turbæ multæ ut audirent, et curarentur ab infirmitatibus suis.
text_pt: A sua fama, porém, se propagava ainda mais, e ajuntava-se muita gente para o ouvir e para ser por ele curada das suas enfermidades.
text_el: διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν:

text_en: And he retired into the desert ; and prayed .
text_la: Ipse autem secedebat in desertum, et orabat.
text_pt: Ele, porém, retirava-se para os desertos, e ali orava.
text_el: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.

text_en: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he sat teaching, that there were also Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, that had come out of every town of Galilee and Judea and Jerusalem : and the power of the Lord was to heal them.
text_la: Et factum est in una dierum, et ipse sedebat docens. Et erant pharisæi sedentes, et legis doctores, qui venerant ex omni castello Galilææ, et Judææ, et Jerusalem : et virtus Domini erat ad sanandum eos.
text_pt: E aconteceu que, num daqueles dias, estava ensinando, e estavam ali assentados fariseus e doutores da lei, que tinham vindo de todas as aldeias da Galiléia, e da Judéia, e de Jerusalém. E a virtude do Senhor estava ali para os curar.
text_el: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι, οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ: καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν.

text_en: And behold, men brought in a bed a man who had the palsy: and they sought means to bring him in and to lay him before him.
text_la: Et ecce viri portantes in lecto hominem, qui erat paralyticus : et quærebant eum inferre, et ponere ante eum.
text_pt: E eis que uns homens transportaram numa cama um homem que estava paralítico, e procuravam fazê-lo entrar e pô-lo diante dele.
text_el: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι αὐτὸν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in, because of the multitude, they went up upon the roof and let him down through the tiles with his bed into the midst before Jesus .
text_la: Et non invenientes qua parte illum inferrent præ turba, ascenderunt supra tectum, et per tegulas summiserunt eum cum lecto in medium ante Jesum.
text_pt: E, não achando por onde o pudessem levar, por causa da multidão, subiram ao telhado, e por entre as telhas o baixaram com a cama, até ao meio, diante de Jesus.
text_el: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον, ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

text_en: Whose faith when he saw, he said: Man, your sins are forgiven you.
text_la: Quorum fidem ut vidit, dixit : Homo, remittuntur tibi peccata tua.
text_pt: E, vendo ele a fé deles, disse-lhe: Homem, os teus pecados te são perdoados.
text_el: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν: ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.

text_en: And the scribes and Pharisees began to think, saying: Who is this who speaks blasphemies ? Who can forgive sins , but God alone?
text_la: Et cœperunt cogitare scribæ et pharisæi, dicentes : Quis est hic, qui loquitur blasphemias? quis potest dimittere peccata, nisi solus Deus?
text_pt: E os escribas e os fariseus começaram a arrazoar, dizendo: Quem é este que diz blasfêmias? Quem pode perdoar pecados, senão só Deus?
text_el: καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες: τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας; τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ θεός;

text_en: And when Jesus knew their thoughts , answering he said to them: What is it you think in your hearts?
text_la: Ut cognovit autem Jesus cogitationes eorum, respondens, dixit ad illos : Quid cogitatis in cordibus vestris?
text_pt: Jesus, porém, conhecendo os seus pensamentos, respondeu, e disse-lhes: Que arrazoais em vossos corações?
text_el: ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς: τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;

text_en: Which is easier to say: Your sins are forgiven you; or to say: Arise and walk?
text_la: Quid est facilius dicere : Dimittuntur tibi peccata : an dicere : Surge, et ambula?
text_pt: Qual é mais fácil? dizer: Os teus pecados te são perdoados; ou dizer: Levanta-te, e anda?
text_el: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν: ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν: ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;

text_en: But that you may know that the Son of man has the power on earth to forgive sins (he says to the sick of the palsy), I say to you: Arise, take up your bed and go into your house.
text_la: Ut autem sciatis quia Filius hominis habet potestatem in terra dimittendi peccata, (ait paralytico) tibi dico, surge, tolle lectum tuum, et vade in domum tuam.
text_pt: Ora, para que saibais que o Filho do homem tem sobre a terra poder de perdoar pecados (disse ao paralítico), a ti te digo: Levanta-te, toma a tua cama, e vai para tua casa.
text_el: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας, εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ: σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.

text_en: And immediately rising up before them, he took up the bed on which he lay: and he went away to his own house, glorifying God .
text_la: Et confestim consurgens coram illis, tulit lectum in quo jacebat : et abiit in domum suam, magnificans Deum.
text_pt: E, levantando-se logo diante deles, e tomando a cama em que estava deitado, foi para sua casa, glorificando a Deus.
text_el: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφ' ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.

text_en: And all were astonished: and they glorified God . And they were filled with fear, saying: We have seen wonderful things today.
text_la: Et stupor apprehendit omnes, et magnificabant Deum. Et repleti sunt timore, dicentes : Quia vidimus mirabilia hodie.
text_pt: E todos ficaram maravilhados, e glorificaram a Deus; e ficaram cheios de temor, dizendo: Hoje vimos prodígios.
text_el: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.

text_en: And after these things, he went forth and saw a publican named Levi , sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said to him: Follow me.
text_la: Et post hæc exiit, et vidit publicanum nomine Levi, sedentem ad telonium, et ait illi : Sequere me.
text_pt: E, depois disto, saiu, e viu um publicano, chamado Levi, assentado na recebedoria, e disse-lhe: Segue-me.
text_el: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν, καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ: ἀκολούθει μοι.

text_en: And leaving all things, he rose up and followed him.
text_la: Et relictis omnibus, surgens secutus est eum.
text_pt: E ele, deixando tudo, levantou-se e o seguiu.
text_el: καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.

text_en: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: And there was a great company of publicans and of others that were at table with them.
text_la: Et fecit ei convivium magnum Levi in domo sua : et erat turba multa publicanorum, et aliorum qui cum illis erant discumbentes.
text_pt: E fez-lhe Levi um grande banquete em sua casa; e havia ali uma multidão de publicanos e outros que estavam com eles à mesa.
text_el: καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ: καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετ' αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.

text_en: But the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying to his disciples : Why do you eat and drink with publicans and sinners?
text_la: Et murmurabant pharisæi et scribæ eorum, dicentes ad discipulos ejus : Quare cum publicanis et peccatoribus manducatis et bibitis?
text_pt: E os escribas deles, e os fariseus, murmuravam contra os seus discípulos, dizendo: Por que comeis e bebeis com publicanos e pecadores?
text_el: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες: διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;

text_en: And Jesus answering, said to them: They that are whole need not the physician: but they that are sick.
text_la: Et respondens Jesus, dixit ad illos : Non egent qui sani sunt medico, sed qui male habent.
text_pt: E Jesus, respondendo, disse-lhes: Não necessitam de médico os que estão sãos, mas, sim, os que estão enfermos;
text_el: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς [ὁ] Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς: οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες:

text_en: I came not to call the just , but sinners to penance .
text_la: Non veni vocare justos, sed peccatores ad pœnitentiam.
text_pt: Eu não vim chamar os justos, mas, sim, os pecadores, ao arrependimento.
text_el: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.

text_en: And they said to him: Why do the disciples of John fast often and make prayers , and the disciples of the Pharisees in like manner; but yours eat and drink?
text_la: At illi dixerunt ad eum : Quare discipuli Joannis jejunant frequenter, et obsecrationes faciunt, similiter et pharisæorum : tui autem edunt et bibunt?
text_pt: Disseram-lhe, então, eles: Por que jejuam os discípulos de João muitas vezes, e fazem orações, como também os dos fariseus, mas os teus comem e bebem?
text_el: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν: οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.

text_en: To whom he said: Can you make the children of the bridegroom fast whilst the bridegroom is with them?
text_la: Quibus ipse ait : Numquid potestis filios sponsi, dum cum illis est sponsus, facere jejunare?
text_pt: E ele lhes disse: Podeis vós fazer jejuar os filhos das bodas, enquanto o esposo está com eles?
text_el: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς, μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος, ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ' αὐτῶν ἐστιν, ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι;

text_en: But the days will come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them: then shall they fast in those days.
text_la: Venient autem dies, cum ablatus fuerit ab illis sponsus : tunc jejunabunt in illis diebus.
text_pt: Dias virão, porém, em que o esposo lhes será tirado, e então, naqueles dias, jejuarão.
text_el: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι, καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ' αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

text_en: And he spoke also a similitude to them: That no man puts a piece from a new garment upon an old garment: otherwise he both rends the new, and the piece taken from the new agrees not with the old.
text_la: Dicebat autem et similitudinem ad illos : Quia nemo commissuram a novo vestimento immittit in vestimentum vetus : alioquin et novum rumpit, et veteri non convenit commissura a novo.
text_pt: E disse-lhes também uma parábola: Ninguém deita um pedaço de uma roupa nova para a coser em roupa velha, pois romperá a nova e o remendo não condiz com a velha.
text_el: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν: εἰ δὲ μή γε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.

text_en: And no man puts new wine into old bottles: otherwise the new wine will break the bottles; and it will be spilled and the bottles will be lost.
text_la: Et nemo mittit vinum novum in utres veteres : alioquin rumpet vinum novum utres, et ipsum effundetur, et utres peribunt:
text_pt: E ninguém deita vinho novo em odres velhos; de outra sorte o vinho novo romperá os odres, e entornar-se-á o vinho, e os odres se estragarão;
text_el: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς: εἰ δὲ μή γε, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται:

text_en: But new wine must be put into new bottles: and both are preserved.
text_la: sed vinum novum in utres novos mittendum est, et utraque conservantur.
text_pt: Mas o vinho novo deve deitar-se em odres novos, e ambos juntamente se conservarão.
text_el: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον.

text_en: And no man drinking old has presently a mind to new: for he says: The old is better.
text_la: Et nemo bibens vetus, statim vult novum : dicit enim : Vetus melius est.
text_pt: E ninguém tendo bebido o velho quer logo o novo, porque diz: Melhor é o velho.
text_el: [Οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον: λέγει γάρ: ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν].

text_en: And it came to pass on the second first sabbath that, as he went through the corn fields, his disciples plucked the ears and ate, rubbing them in their hands.
text_la: Factum est autem in sabbato secundo, primo, cum transiret per sata, vellebant discipuli ejus spicas, et manducabant confricantes manibus.
text_pt: E aconteceu que, no segundo sábado após o primeiro, passou pelas searas, e os seus discípulos iam arrancando espigas e, esfregando-as com as mãos, as comiam.
text_el: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν διὰ σπορίμων, καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν.

text_en: And some of the Pharisees said to them: Why do you that which is not lawful on the sabbath days ?
text_la: Quidam autem pharisæorum, dicebant illis : Quid facitis quod non licet in sabbatis?
text_pt: E alguns dos fariseus lhes disseram: Por que fazeis o que não é lícito fazer nos sábados?
text_el: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν: τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν;

text_en: And Jesus answering them, said: Have you not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was hungry and they that were with him:
text_la: Et respondens Jesus ad eos, dixit : Nec hoc legistis quod fecit David, cum esurisset ipse, et qui cum illo erant?
text_pt: E Jesus, respondendo-lhes, disse: Nunca lestes o que fez Davi quando teve fome, ele e os que com ele estavam?
text_el: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν [ὁ] Ἰησοῦς: οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ' αὐτοῦ [ὄντες];

text_en: How he went into the house of God and took and ate the bread of proposition and gave to them that were with him, which is not lawful to eat but only for the priests ?
text_la: quomodo intravit in domum Dei, et panes propositionis sumpsit, et manducavit, et dedit his qui cum ipso erant : quos non licet manducare nisi tantum sacerdotibus?
text_pt: Como entrou na casa de Deus, e tomou os pães da proposição, e os comeu, e deu também aos que estavam com ele, os quais não é lícito comer senão só aos sacerdotes?
text_el: ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ' αὐτοῦ, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς;

text_en: And he said to them: The Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath .
text_la: Et dicebat illis : Quia dominus est Filius hominis etiam sabbati.
text_pt: E dizia-lhes: O Filho do homem é Senhor até do sábado.
text_el: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς κύριός ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

text_en: And it came to pass also, on another sabbath , that he entered into the synagogue and taught. And there was a man whose right hand was withered.
text_la: Factum est autem in alio sabbato, ut intraret in synagogam, et doceret. Et erat ibi homo, et manus ejus dextra erat arida.
text_pt: E aconteceu também noutro sábado, que entrou na sinagoga, e estava ensinando; e havia ali um homem que tinha a mão direita mirrada.
text_el: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν. καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά:

text_en: And the scribes and Pharisees watched if he would heal on the sabbath : that they might find an accusation against him.
text_la: Observabant autem scribæ et pharisæi si in sabbato curaret, ut invenirent unde accusarent eum.
text_pt: E os escribas e fariseus observavam-no, se o curaria no sábado, para acharem de que o acusar.
text_el: παρετηροῦντο δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεύει, ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.

text_en: But he knew their thoughts and said to the man who had the withered hand: Arise and stand forth in the midst. And rising he stood forth.
text_la: Ipse vero sciebat cogitationes eorum : et ait homini qui habebat manum aridam : Surge, et sta in medium. Et surgens stetit.
text_pt: Mas ele bem conhecia os seus pensamentos; e disse ao homem que tinha a mão mirrada: Levanta-te, e fica em pé no meio. E, levantando-se ele, ficou em pé.
text_el: αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν: εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα: ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον. καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη.

text_en: Then Jesus said to them: I ask you, if it be lawful on the sabbath days to do good or to do evil ? To save life or to destroy?
text_la: Ait autem ad illos Jesus : Interrogo vos si licet sabbatis benefacere, an male : animam salvam facere, an perdere?
text_pt: Então Jesus lhes disse: Uma coisa vos hei de perguntar: É lícito nos sábados fazer bem, ou fazer mal? salvar a vida, ou matar?
text_el: εἶπεν δὲ [ὁ] Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς: ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς, εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀπολέσαι.

text_en: And looking round about on them all, he said to the man : Stretch forth your hand. And he stretched it forth. And his hand was restored.
text_la: Et circumspectis omnibus dixit homini : Extende manum tuam. Et extendit : et restituta est manus ejus.
text_pt: E, olhando para todos em redor, disse ao homem: Estende a tua mão. E ele assim o fez, e a mão lhe foi restituída sã como a outra.
text_el: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ: ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου. ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And they were filled with madness : and they talked one with another, what they might do to Jesus .
text_la: Ipsi autem repleti sunt insipientia, et colloquebantur ad invicem, quidnam facerent Jesu.
text_pt: E ficaram cheios de furor, e uns com os outros conferenciavam sobre o que fariam a Jesus.
text_el: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας, καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

text_en: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray : and he passed the whole night in the prayer of God .
text_la: Factum est autem in illis diebus, exiit in montem orare, et erat pernoctans in oratione Dei.
text_pt: E aconteceu que naqueles dias subiu ao monte a orar, e passou a noite em oração a Deus.
text_el: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι, καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ.

text_en: And when day had come, he called unto him his disciples : and he chose twelve of them (whom also he named apostles ):
text_la: Et cum dies factus esset, vocavit discipulos suos : et elegit duodecim ex ipsis (quos et apostolos nominavit):
text_pt: E, quando já era dia, chamou a si os seus discípulos, e escolheu doze deles, a quem também deu o nome de apóstolos:
text_el: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπ' αὐτῶν δώδεκα, οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν,

text_en: Simon , whom he surnamed Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John , Philip and Bartholomew ,
text_la: Simonem, quem cognominavit Petrum, et Andream fratrem ejus, Jacobum, et Joannem, Philippum, et Bartholomæum,
text_pt: Simão, ao qual também chamou Pedro, e André, seu irmão; Tiago e João; Filipe e Bartolomeu;
text_el: Σίμωνα, ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον, καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον

text_en: Matthew and Thomas , James the son of Alpheus , and Simon who is called Zelotes ,
text_la: Matthæum, et Thomam, Jacobum Alphæi, et Simonem, qui vocatur Zelotes,
text_pt: Mateus e Tomé; Tiago, filho de Alfeu, e Simão, chamado Zelote;
text_el: καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν, [καὶ] Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου, καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν,

text_en: and Jude the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot , who was the traitor.
text_la: et Judam Jacobi, et Judam Iscariotem, qui fuit proditor.
text_pt: E Judas, irmão de Tiago, e Judas Iscariotes, que foi o traidor.
text_el: καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριώθ, ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης.

text_en: And coming down with them, he stood in a plain place: and the company of his disciples and a very great multitude of people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast, both of Tyre and Sidon ,
text_la: Et descendens cum illis, stetit in loco campestri, et turba discipulorum ejus, et multitudo copiosa plebis ab omni Judæa, et Jerusalem, et maritima, et Tyri, et Sidonis,
text_pt: E, descendo com eles, parou num lugar plano, e também um grande número de seus discípulos, e grande multidão de povo de toda a Judéia, e de Jerusalém, e da costa marítima de Tiro e de Sidom; os quais tinham vindo para o ouvir, e serem curados das suas enfermidades,
text_el: καὶ καταβὰς μετ' αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ, καὶ ὄχλος πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος,

text_en: who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases. And they that were troubled with unclean spirits were cured.
text_la: qui venerant ut audirent eum, et sanarentur a languoribus suis. Et qui vexabantur a spiritibus immundis, curabantur.
text_pt: Como também os atormentados dos espíritos imundos; e eram curados.
text_el: οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν, καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο:

text_en: And all the multitude sought to touch him: for virtue went out from him and healed all.
text_la: Et omnis turba quærebat eum tangere : quia virtus de illo exibat, et sanabat omnes.
text_pt: E toda a multidão procurava tocar-lhe, porque saía dele virtude, e curava a todos.
text_el: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δύναμις παρ' αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας.

text_en: And he, lifting up his eyes on his disciples , said: Blessed are you poor: for yours is the kingdom of God .
text_la: Et ipse elevatis oculis in discipulis suis, dicebat : Beati pauperes, quia vestrum est regnum Dei.
text_pt: E, levantando ele os olhos para os seus discípulos, dizia: Bem-aventurados vós, os pobres, porque vosso é o reino de Deus.
text_el: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν: μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί, ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

text_en: Blessed are you that hunger now: for you shall be filled. Blessed are you that weep now: for you shall laugh.
text_la: Beati qui nunc esuritis, quia saturabimini. Beati qui nunc fletis, quia ridebitis.
text_pt: Bem-aventurados vós, que agora tendes fome, porque sereis fartos. Bem-aventurados vós, que agora chorais, porque haveis de rir.
text_el: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν, ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε. μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν, ὅτι γελάσετε.

text_en: Blessed shall you be when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you and shall reproach you and cast out your name as evil , for the Son of man's sake.
text_la: Beati eritis cum vos oderint homines, et cum separaverint vos, et exprobraverint, et ejicerint nomen vestrum tamquam malum propter Filium hominis.
text_pt: Bem-aventurados sereis quando os homens vos odiarem e quando vos separarem, e vos injuriarem, e rejeitarem o vosso nome como mau, por causa do Filho do homem.
text_el: μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι, καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου:

text_en: Be glad in that day and rejoice: for behold, your reward is great in heaven , For according to these things did their fathers to the prophets .
text_la: Gaudete in illa die, et exsultate : ecce enim merces vestra multa est in cælo : secundum hæc enim faciebant prophetis patres eorum.
text_pt: Folgai nesse dia, exultai; porque eis que é grande o vosso galardão no céu, pois assim faziam os seus pais aos profetas.
text_el: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ: κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.

text_en: But woe to you that are rich: for you have your consolation.
text_la: Verumtamen væ vobis divitibus, quia habetis consolationem vestram.
text_pt: Mas ai de vós, ricos! porque já tendes a vossa consolação.
text_el: Πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις, ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν.

text_en: Woe to you that are filled: for you shall hunger. Woe to you that now laugh: for you shall mourn and weep.
text_la: Væ vobis, qui saturati estis : quia esurietis. Væ vobis, qui ridetis nunc : quia lugebitis et flebitis.
text_pt: Ai de vós, os que estais fartos, porque tereis fome. Ai de vós, os que agora rides, porque vos lamentareis e chorareis.
text_el: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι νῦν, ὅτι πεινάσετε. οὐαί, οἱ γελῶντες νῦν, ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε.

text_en: Woe to you when men shall bless you: for according to these things did their fathers to the false prophets .
text_la: Væ cum benedixerint vobis homines : secundum hæc enim faciebant pseudoprophetis patres eorum.
text_pt: Ai de vós quando todos os homens de vós disserem bem, porque assim faziam seus pais aos falsos profetas.
text_el: οὐαὶ ὅταν καλῶς ὑμᾶς εἴπωσιν πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι: κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.

text_en: But I say to you that hear: Love your enemies. Do good to them that hate you.
text_la: Sed vobis dico, qui auditis : diligite inimicos vestros, benefacite his qui oderunt vos.
text_pt: Mas a vós, que isto ouvis, digo: Amai a vossos inimigos, fazei bem aos que vos odeiam;
text_el: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς,

text_en: Bless them that curse you and pray for them that calumniate you.
text_la: Benedicite maledicentibus vobis, et orate pro calumniantibus vos.
text_pt: Bendizei os que vos maldizem, e orai pelos que vos caluniam.
text_el: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς, προσεύχεσθε περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς.

text_en: And to him that strikes you on the one cheek, offer also the other. And him that takes away from you your cloak, forbid not to take your coat also.
text_la: Et qui te percutit in maxillam, præbe et alteram. Et ab eo qui aufert tibi vestimentum, etiam tunicam noli prohibere.
text_pt: Ao que te ferir numa face, oferece-lhe também a outra; e ao que te houver tirado a capa, nem a túnica recuses;
text_el: τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς.

text_en: Give to every one that asks you: and of him that takes away your goods, ask them not again.
text_la: Omni autem petenti te, tribue : et qui aufert quæ tua sunt, ne repetas.
text_pt: E dá a qualquer que te pedir; e ao que tomar o que é teu, não lho tornes a pedir.
text_el: παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει.

text_en: And as you would that men should do to you, do you also to them in like manner.
text_la: Et prout vultis ut faciant vobis homines, et vos facite illis similiter.
text_pt: E como vós quereis que os homens vos façam, da mesma maneira lhes fazei vós, também.
text_el: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.

text_en: And if you love them that love you, what thanks are to you? For sinners also love those that love them.
text_la: Et si diligitis eos qui vos diligunt, quæ vobis est gratia? nam et peccatores diligentes se diligunt.
text_pt: E se amardes aos que vos amam, que recompensa tereis? Também os pecadores amam aos que os amam.
text_el: καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν.

text_en: And if you do good to them who do good to you, what thanks are to you? For sinners also do this.
text_la: Et si benefeceritis his qui vobis benefaciunt, quæ vobis est gratia? siquidem et peccatores hoc faciunt.
text_pt: E se fizerdes bem aos que vos fazem bem, que recompensa tereis? Também os pecadores fazem o mesmo.
text_el: καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν.

text_en: And if you lend to them of whom you hope to receive, what thanks are to you? For sinners also lend to sinners, for to receive as much.
text_la: Et si mutuum dederitis his a quibus speratis recipere, quæ gratia est vobis? nam et peccatores peccatoribus fœnerantur, ut recipiant æqualia.
text_pt: E se emprestardes àqueles de quem esperais tornar a receber, que recompensa tereis? Também os pecadores emprestam aos pecadores, para tornarem a receber outro tanto.
text_el: καὶ ἐὰν δανίσητε παρ' ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα.

text_en: But love your enemies: do good , and lend, hoping for nothing thereby: and your reward shall be great, and you shall be the sons of the Highest. For he is kind to the unthankful and to the evil .
text_la: Verumtamen diligite inimicos vestros : benefacite, et mutuum date, nihil inde sperantes : et erit merces vestra multa, et eritis filii Altissimi, quia ipse benignus est super ingratos et malos.
text_pt: Amai, pois, a vossos inimigos, e fazei bem, e emprestai, sem nada esperardes, e será grande o vosso galardão, e sereis filhos do Altíssimo; porque ele é benigno até para com os ingratos e maus.
text_el: Πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες: καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς, καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ ὑψίστου, ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς.

text_en: Be therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
text_la: Estote ergo misericordes sicut et Pater vester misericors est.
text_pt: Sede, pois, misericordiosos, como também vosso Pai é misericordioso.
text_el: γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες, καθὼς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν.

text_en: Judge not: and you shall not be judged. Condemn not: and you shall not be condemned. Forgive: and you shall be forgiven.
text_la: Nolite judicare, et non judicabimini : nolite condemnare, et non condemnabimini. Dimitte, et dimittemini.
text_pt: Não julgueis, e não sereis julgados; não condeneis, e não sereis condenados; soltai, e soltar-vos-ão.
text_el: καὶ μὴ κρίνετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε: καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε. ἀπολύετε, καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε:

text_en: Give: and it shall be given to you: good measure and pressed down and shaken together and running over shall they give into your bosom. For with the same measure that you shall mete withal, it shall be measured to you again.
text_la: Date, et dabitur vobis : mensuram bonam, et confertam, et coagitatam, et supereffluentem dabunt in sinum vestrum. Eadem quippe mensura, qua mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis.
text_pt: Dai, e ser-vos-á dado; boa medida, recalcada, sacudida e transbordando, vos deitarão no vosso regaço; porque com a mesma medida com que medirdes também vos medirão de novo.
text_el: δίδοτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν: μέτρον καλὸν πεπιεσμένον σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς τὸν κόλπον ὑμῶν: ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.

text_en: And he spoke also to them a similitude: Can the blind lead the blind? Do they not both fall into the ditch?
text_la: Dicebat autem illis et similitudinem : Numquid potest cæcus cæcum ducere? nonne ambo in foveam cadunt?
text_pt: E dizia-lhes uma parábola: Pode porventura o cego guiar o cego? Não cairão ambos na cova?
text_el: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς. μήτι δύναται τυφλὸς τυφλὸν ὁδηγεῖν; οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον ἐμπεσοῦνται;

text_en: The disciple is not above his master: but every one shall be perfect, if he be as his master.
text_la: Non est discipulus super magistrum : perfectus autem omnis erit, si sit sicut magister ejus.
text_pt: O discípulo não é superior a seu mestre, mas todo o que for perfeito será como o seu mestre.
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον: κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And why do you see the mote in your brother's eye: but the beam that is in your own eye you consider not?
text_la: Quid autem vides festucam in oculo fratris tui, trabem autem, quæ in oculo tuo est, non consideras?
text_pt: E por que atentas tu no argueiro que está no olho de teu irmão, e não reparas na trave que está no teu próprio olho?
text_el: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς;

text_en: Or how can you say to your brother: Brother, let me pull the mote out of your eye, when you yourself see not the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite , cast first the beam out of your own eye: and then shall you see clearly to take out the mote from your brother's eye.
text_la: aut quomodo potes dicere fratri tuo : Frater, sine ejiciam festucam de oculo tuo : ipse in oculo tuo trabem non videns? Hypocrita, ejice primum trabem de oculo tuo : et tunc perspicies ut educas festucam de oculo fratris tui.
text_pt: Ou como podes dizer a teu irmão: Irmão, deixa-me tirar o argueiro que está no teu olho, não atentando tu mesmo na trave que está no teu olho? Hipócrita, tira primeiro a trave do teu olho, e então verás bem para tirar o argueiro que está no olho de teu irmão.
text_el: πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου: ἀδελφέ, ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου, αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων; ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν.

text_en: For there is no good tree that brings forth evil fruit: nor an evil tree that brings forth good fruit.
text_la: Non est enim arbor bona, quæ facit fructus malos : neque arbor mala, faciens fructum bonum.
text_pt: Porque não há boa árvore que dê mau fruto, nem má árvore que dê bom fruto.
text_el: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν, οὐδὲ πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν.

text_en: For every tree is known by its fruit. For men do not gather figs from thorns: nor from a bramble bush do they gather the grape.
text_la: Unaquæque enim arbor de fructu suo cognoscitur. Neque enim de spinis colligunt ficus : neque de rubo vindemiant uvam.
text_pt: Porque cada árvore se conhece pelo seu próprio fruto; pois não se colhem figos dos espinheiros, nem se vindimam uvas dos abrolhos.
text_el: ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται: οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα, οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν.

text_en: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth that which is good : and an evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth that which is evil . For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
text_la: Bonus homo de bono thesauro cordis sui profert bonum : et malus homo de malo thesauro profert malum. Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur.
text_pt: O homem bom, do bom tesouro do seu coração tira o bem, e o homem mau, do mau tesouro do seu coração tira o mal, porque da abundância do seu coração fala a boca.
text_el: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν: ἐκ γὰρ περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And why call you me, Lord, Lord; and do not the things which I say?
text_la: Quid autem vocatis me Domine, Domine : et non facitis quæ dico?
text_pt: E por que me chamais, Senhor, Senhor, e não fazeis o que eu digo?
text_el: Τί δέ με καλεῖτε, κύριε κύριε, καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;

text_en: Every one that comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you to whom he is like.
text_la: Omnis qui venit ad me, et audit sermones meos, et facit eos, ostendam vobis cui similis sit:
text_pt: Qualquer que vem a mim e ouve as minhas palavras, e as observa, eu vos mostrarei a quem é semelhante:
text_el: πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς, ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος:

text_en: He is like to a man building a house, who digged deep and laid the foundation upon a rock. And when a flood came, the stream beat vehemently upon that house: and it could not shake it: for it was founded on a rock.
text_la: similis est homini ædificanti domum, qui fodit in altum, et posuit fundamentum super petram : inundatione autem facta, illisum est flumen domui illi, et non potuit eam movere : fundata enim erat super petram.
text_pt: É semelhante ao homem que edificou uma casa, e cavou, e abriu bem fundo, e pôs os alicerces sobre a rocha; e, vindo a enchente, bateu com ímpeto a corrente naquela casa, e não a pôde abalar, porque estava fundada sobre a rocha.
text_el: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν, ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν: πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν.

text_en: But he that hears and does not is like to a man building his house upon the earth without a foundation: against which the stream beat vehemently. And immediately it fell: and the ruin of that house was great.
text_la: Qui autem audit, et non facit, similis est homini ædificanti domum suam super terram sine fundamento : in quam illisus est fluvius, et continuo cecidit : et facta est ruina domus illius magna.
text_pt: Mas o que ouve e não pratica é semelhante ao homem que edificou uma casa sobre terra, sem alicerces, na qual bateu com ímpeto a corrente, e logo caiu; e foi grande a ruína daquela casa.
text_el: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου, ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός, καὶ εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν, καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα.

text_en: And when he had finished all his words in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capharnaum .
text_la: Cum autem implesset omnia verba sua in aures plebis, intravit Capharnaum.
text_pt: E, depois de concluir todos estes discursos perante o povo, entrou em Cafarnaum.
text_el: Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.

text_en: And the servant of a certain centurion who was dear to him, being sick, was ready to die.
text_la: Centurionis autem cujusdam servus male habens, erat moriturus : qui illi erat pretiosus.
text_pt: E o servo de um certo centurião, a quem muito estimava, estava doente, e moribundo.
text_el: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.

text_en: And when he had heard of Jesus , he sent unto him the ancients of the Jews , desiring him to come and heal his servant.
text_la: Et cum audisset de Jesu, misit ad eum seniores Judæorum, rogans eum ut veniret et salvaret servum ejus.
text_pt: E, quando ouviu falar de Jesus, enviou-lhe uns anciãos dos judeus, rogando-lhe que viesse curar o seu servo.
text_el: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And when they came to Jesus , they besought him earnestly, saying to him: He is worthy that you should do this for him.
text_la: At illi cum venissent ad Jesum, rogabant eum sollicite, dicentes ei : Quia dignus est ut hoc illi præstes:
text_pt: E, chegando eles junto de Jesus, rogaram-lhe muito, dizendo: É digno de que lhe concedas isto,
text_el: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως, λέγοντες ὅτι ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ παρέξῃ τοῦτο:

text_en: For he loves our nation: and he has built us a synagogue .
text_la: diligit enim gentem nostram, et synagogam ipse ædificavit nobis.
text_pt: Porque ama a nossa nação, e ele mesmo nos edificou a sinagoga.
text_el: ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν, καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.

text_en: And Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent his friends to him, saying: Lord, trouble not yourself; for I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof.
text_la: Jesus autem ibat cum illis. Et cum jam non longe esset a domo, misit ad eum centurio amicos, dicens : Domine, noli vexari : non enim sum dignus ut sub tectum meum intres:
text_pt: E foi Jesus com eles; mas, quando já estava perto da casa, enviou-lhe o centurião uns amigos, dizendo-lhe: Senhor, não te incomodes, porque não sou digno de que entres debaixo do meu telhado.
text_el: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς. ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης λέγων: αὐτῷ κύριε, μὴ σκύλλου: οὐ γὰρ ἱκανός εἰμι ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς:

text_en: For which cause neither did I think myself worthy to come to you: but say the word, and my servant shall be healed.
text_la: propter quod et meipsum non sum dignum arbitratus ut venirem ad te : sed dic verbo, et sanabitur puer meus.
text_pt: E por isso nem ainda me julguei digno de ir ter contigo; dize, porém, uma palavra, e o meu criado sarará.
text_el: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν: ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου.

text_en: For I also am a man subject to authority, having under me soldiers: and I say to one, Go, and he goes: and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
text_la: Nam et ego homo sum sub potestate constitutus, habens sub me milites : et dico huic, Vade, et vadit : et alii, Veni, et venit : et servo meo, Fac hoc, et facit.
text_pt: Porque também eu sou homem sujeito à autoridade, e tenho soldados sob o meu poder, e digo a este: Vai, e ele vai; e a outro: Vem, e ele vem; e ao meu servo: Faze isto, e ele o faz.
text_el: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ἔχων ὑπ' ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ, πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ: ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου: ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.

text_en: Which Jesus hearing, marvelled: and turning about to the multitude that followed him, he said: Amen I say to you, I have not found so great faith , not even in Israel .
text_la: Quo audito Jesus miratus est : et conversus sequentibus se turbis, dixit : Amen dico vobis, nec in Israël tantam fidem inveni.
text_pt: E, ouvindo isto Jesus, maravilhou-se dele, e voltando-se, disse à multidão que o seguia: Digo-vos que nem ainda em Israel tenho achado tanta fé.
text_el: ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν: λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον.

text_en: And they who were sent, being returned to the house, found the servant whole who had been sick.
text_la: Et reversi, qui missi fuerant, domum, invenerunt servum, qui languerat, sanum.
text_pt: E, voltando para casa os que foram enviados, acharam são o servo enfermo.
text_el: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες εὗρον τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα.

text_en: And it came to pass afterwards that he went into a city that is called Naim : and there went with him his disciples and a great multitude.
text_la: Et factum est : deinceps ibat in civitatem quæ vocatur Naim : et ibant cum eo discipuli ejus et turba copiosa.
text_pt: E aconteceu que, no dia seguinte, ele foi à cidade chamada Naim, e com ele iam muitos dos seus discípulos, e uma grande multidão;
text_el: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.

text_en: And when he came near to the gate of the city, behold a dead man was carried out, the only son of his mother: and she was a widow . And a great multitude of the city was with her.
text_la: Cum autem appropinquaret portæ civitatis, ecce defunctus efferebatur filius unicus matris suæ : et hæc vidua erat : et turba civitatis multa cum illa.
text_pt: E, quando chegou perto da porta da cidade, eis que levavam um defunto, filho único de sua mãe, que era viúva; e com ela ia uma grande multidão da cidade.
text_el: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς μονογενὴς υἱὸς τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὴ ἦν χήρα, καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ.

text_en: Whom when the Lord had seen, being moved with mercy towards her, he said to her: Weep not.
text_la: Quam cum vidisset Dominus, misericordia motus super eam, dixit illi : Noli flere.
text_pt: E, vendo-a, o Senhor moveu-se de íntima compaixão por ela, e disse-lhe: Não chores.
text_el: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ' αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ: μὴ κλαῖε.

text_en: And he came near and touched the bier. And they that carried it stood still. And he said: Young man , I say to you, arise.
text_la: Et accessit, et tetigit loculum. (Hi autem qui portabant, steterunt.) Et ait : Adolescens, tibi dico, surge.
text_pt: E, chegando-se, tocou o esquife (e os que o levavam pararam), e disse: Jovem, a ti te digo: Levanta-te. E o que fora defunto assentou-se, e começou a falar.
text_el: καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ, οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν, καὶ εἶπεν: νεανίσκε, σοὶ λέγω, ἐγέρθητι.

text_en: And he that was dead sat up and begun to speak. And he gave him to his mother.
text_la: Et resedit qui erat mortuus, et cœpit loqui. Et dedit illum matri suæ.
text_pt: E entregou-o à sua mãe.
text_el: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And there came a fear upon them all: and they glorified God saying: A great prophet is risen up among us: and, God has visited his people.
text_la: Accepit autem omnes timor : et magnificabant Deum, dicentes : Quia propheta magnus surrexit in nobis : et quia Deus visitavit plebem suam.
text_pt: E de todos se apoderou o temor, e glorificavam a Deus, dizendo: Um grande profeta se levantou entre nós, e Deus visitou o seu povo.
text_el: ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅτι ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judea and throughout all the country round about.
text_la: Et exiit hic sermo in universam Judæam de eo, et in omnem circa regionem.
text_pt: E correu dele esta fama por toda a Judéia e por toda a terra circunvizinha.
text_el: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ.

text_en: And John's disciples told him of all these things.
text_la: Et nuntiaverunt Joanni discipuli ejus de omnibus his.
text_pt: E os discípulos de João anunciaram-lhe todas estas coisas.
text_el: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων. καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης

text_en: And John called to him two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus , saying: Are you he that is to come ? Or look we for another?
text_la: Et convocavit duos de discipulis suis Joannes, et misit ad Jesum, dicens : Tu es qui venturus es, an alium exspectamus?
text_pt: E João, chamando dois dos seusdiscípulos, enviou-os a Jesus, dizendo: És tu aquele que havia de vir, ou esperamos outro?
text_el: ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον λέγων: σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἕτερον προσδοκῶμεν;

text_en: And when the men had come unto him, they said: John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying: Are you he that is to come ? Or look we for another?
text_la: Cum autem venissent ad eum viri, dixerunt : Joannes Baptista misit nos ad te dicens : Tu es qui venturus es, an alium exspectamus?
text_pt: E, quando aqueles homens chegaram junto dele, disseram: João o Batista enviou-nos a perguntar-te: És tu aquele que havia de vir, ou esperamos outro?
text_el: παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν: Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων: σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;

text_en: (And in that same hour, he cured many of their diseases and hurts and evil spirits : and to many that were blind he gave sight.)
text_la: (In ipsa autem hora multos curavit a languoribus, et plagis, et spiritibus malis, et cæcis multis donavit visum.)
text_pt: E, na mesma hora, curou muitos de enfermidades, e males, e espíritos maus, e deu vista a muitos cegos.
text_el: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν, καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν.

text_en: And answering, he said to them: Go and relate to John what you have heard and seen: the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are made clean, the deaf hear, the dead rise again, to the poor the gospel is preached.
text_la: Et respondens, dixit illis : Euntes renuntiate Joanni quæ audistis et vidistis : quia cæci vident, claudi ambulant, leprosi mundantur, surdi audiunt, mortui resurgunt, pauperes evangelizantur:
text_pt: Respondendo, então, Jesus, disse-lhes: Ide, e anunciai a João o que tendes visto e ouvido: que os cegos vêem, os coxos andam, os leprosos são purificados, os surdos ouvem, os mortos ressuscitam e aos pobres anuncia-se o evangelho.
text_el: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς: πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε, τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν χωλοὶ, περιπατοῦσιν λεπροὶ, καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται, πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται:

text_en: And blessed is he whosoever shall not be scandalized in me.
text_la: et beatus est quicumque non fuerit scandalizatus in me.
text_pt: E bem-aventurado é aquele que em mim se não escandalizar.
text_el: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.

text_en: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak to the multitudes concerning John . What did you go out into the desert to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
text_la: Et cum discessissent nuntii Joannis, cœpit de Joanne dicere ad turbas : Quid existis in desertum videre? arundinem vento agitatam?
text_pt: E, tendo-se retirado os mensageiros de João, começou a dizer à multidão acerca de João: Que saístes a ver no deserto? uma cana abalada pelo vento?
text_el: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους περὶ Ἰωάννου: τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι; κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;

text_en: But what went you out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold they that are in costly apparel and live delicately are in the houses of kings.
text_la: Sed quid existis videre? hominem mollibus vestibus indutum? Ecce qui in veste pretiosa sunt et deliciis, in domibus regum sunt.
text_pt: Mas que saístes a ver? um homem trajado de vestes delicadas? Eis que os que andam com preciosas vestiduras, e em delícias, estão nos paços reais.
text_el: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον; ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν.

text_en: But what went you out to see? A prophet ? Yea, I say to you, and more than a prophet .
text_la: Sed quid existis videre? prophetam? Utique dico vobis, et plus quam prophetam:
text_pt: Mas que saístes a ver? um profeta? Sim, vos digo, e muito mais do que profeta.
text_el: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; προφήτην; ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.

text_en: This is he of whom it is written: Behold I send my angel before your face, who shall prepare your way before you.
text_la: hic est, de quo scriptum est : Ecce mitto angelum meum ante faciem tuam, qui præparabit viam tuam ante te.
text_pt: Este é aquele de quem está escrito: Eis que envio o meu anjo diante da tua face, O qual preparará diante de ti o teu caminho.
text_el: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται: ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.

text_en: For I say to you: Amongst those that are born of men , there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist . But he that is the lesser in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
text_la: Dico enim vobis : major inter natos mulierum propheta Joanne Baptista nemo est : qui autem minor est in regno Dei, major est illo.
text_pt: E eu vos digo que, entre os nascidos de mulheres, não há maior profeta do que João o Batista; mas o menor no reino de Deus é maior do que ele.
text_el: λέγω ὑμῖν, μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν: ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.

text_en: And all the people hearing, and the publicans , justified God , being baptized with John's baptism .
text_la: Et omnis populus audiens et publicani, justificaverunt Deum, baptizati baptismo Joannis.
text_pt: E todo o povo que o ouviu e os publicanos, tendo sido batizados com o batismo de João, justificaram a Deus.
text_el: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν, βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου:

text_en: But the Pharisees and the lawyers despised the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized by him.
text_la: Pharisæi autem et legisperiti consilium Dei spreverunt in semetipsos, non baptizati ab eo.
text_pt: Mas os fariseus e os doutores da lei rejeitaram o conselho de Deus contra si mesmos, não tendo sido batizados por ele.
text_el: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπ' αὐτοῦ.

text_en: And the Lord said: Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation ? And to what are they like?
text_la: Ait autem Dominus : Cui ergo similes dicam homines generationis hujus? et cui similes sunt?
text_pt: E disse o Senhor: A quem, pois, compararei os homens desta geração, e a quem são semelhantes?
text_el: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;

text_en: They are like to children sitting in the marketplace and speaking one to another and saying: We have piped to you, and you have not danced : we have mourned, and you have not wept.
text_la: Similes sunt pueris sedentibus in foro, et loquentibus ad invicem, et dicentibus : Cantavimus vobis tibiis, et non saltastis : lamentavimus, et non plorastis.
text_pt: São semelhantes aos meninos que, assentados nas praças, clamam uns aos outros, e dizem: Tocamo-vos flauta, e não dançastes; cantamo-vos lamentações, e não chorastes.
text_el: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ἃ λέγει: ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε, ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε.

text_en: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine. And you say: He has a devil .
text_la: Venit enim Joannes Baptista, neque manducans panem, neque bibens vinum, et dicitis : Dæmonium habet.
text_pt: Porque veio João o Batista, que não comia pão nem bebia vinho, e dizeis: Tem demônio;
text_el: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον, καὶ λέγετε: δαιμόνιον ἔχει.

text_en: The Son of man has come eating and drinking. And you say: Behold a man that is a glutton and a drinker of wine, a friend of publicans and sinners.
text_la: Venit Filius hominis manducans, et bibens, et dicitis : Ecce homo devorator, et bibens vinum, amicus publicanorum et peccatorum.
text_pt: Veio o Filho do homem, que come e bebe, e dizeis: Eis aí um homem comilão e bebedor de vinho, amigo dos publicanos e pecadores.
text_el: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγετε: ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.

text_en: And wisdom is justified by all her children.
text_la: Et justificata est sapientia ab omnibus filiis suis.
text_pt: Mas a sabedoria é justificada por todos os seus filhos.
text_el: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς.

text_en: And one of the Pharisees desired him to eat with him. And he went into the house of the Pharisee and sat down to meat.
text_la: Rogabat autem illum quidam de pharisæis ut manducaret cum illo. Et ingressus domum pharisæi discubuit.
text_pt: E rogou-lhe um dos fariseus que comesse com ele; e, entrando em casa do fariseu, assentou-se à mesa.
text_el: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετ' αὐτοῦ: καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη.

text_en: And behold a woman that was in the city, a sinner, when she knew that he sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment .
text_la: Et ecce mulier, quæ erat in civitate peccatrix, ut cognovit quod accubuisset in domo pharisæi, attulit alabastrum unguenti:
text_pt: E eis que uma mulher da cidade, uma pecadora, sabendo que ele estava à mesa em casa do fariseu, levou um vaso de alabastro com ungüento;
text_el: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός, καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου

text_en: And standing behind at his feet she began to wash his feet with tears and wiped them with the hairs of her head and kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment .
text_la: et stans retro secus pedes ejus, lacrimis cœpit rigare pedes ejus, et capillis capitis sui tergebat, et osculabatur pedes ejus, et unguento ungebat.
text_pt: E, estando por detrás, aos seus pés, chorando, começou a regar-lhe os pés com lágrimas, e enxugava-lhos com os cabelos da sua cabeça; e beijava-lhe os pés, e ungia-lhos com o ungüento.
text_el: καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα, τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.

text_en: And the Pharisee , who had invited him, seeing it, spoke within himself, saying: This man , if he were if a prophet , would know surely who and what manner of woman this is that touches him, that she is a sinner.
text_la: Videns autem pharisæus, qui vocaverat eum, ait intra se dicens : Hic si esset propheta, sciret utique quæ et qualis est mulier, quæ tangit eum : quia peccatrix est.
text_pt: Quando isto viu o fariseu que o tinha convidado, falava consigo, dizendo: Se este fora profeta, bem saberia quem e qual é a mulher que lhe tocou, pois é uma pecadora.
text_el: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων: οὗτος εἰ ἦν [ὁ] προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.

text_en: And Jesus answering, said to him: Simon, I have somewhat to say to you. But he said: Master, say it.
text_la: Et respondens Jesus, dixit ad illum : Simon, habeo tibi aliquid dicere. At ille ait : Magister, dic.
text_pt: E respondendo, Jesus disse-lhe: Simão, uma coisa tenho a dizer-te. E ele disse: Dize-a, Mestre.
text_el: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν: Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν. ὁ δέ: διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν.

text_en: A certain creditor had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence and the other fifty.
text_la: Duo debitores erant cuidam fœneratori : unus debebat denarios quingentos, et alius quinquaginta.
text_pt: Um certo credor tinha dois devedores: um devia-lhe quinhentos dinheiros, e outro cinqüenta.
text_el: Δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι: ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.

text_en: And whereas they had not wherewith to pay, he forgave them both. Which therefore of the two loves him most?
text_la: Non habentibus illis unde redderent, donavit utrisque. Quis ergo eum plus diligit?
text_pt: E, não tendo eles com que pagar, perdoou-lhes a ambos. Dize, pois, qual deles o amará mais?
text_el: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο. τίς οὖν αὐτῶν πλεῖον ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν;

text_en: Simon answering, said: I suppose that he to whom he forgave most. And he said to him: You have judged rightly.
